answer: A durable defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: every agent locks a small refundable deposit before it can trade, and its past work accrues as a reputation signal that decays if it goes idle. A fake identity starts with zero history, so a sybil swarm must pay the deposit for each copy and wait weeks to build trust, while one honest agent's record compounds. Old verified work becomes a relic of proven behavior that cannot be bought, and the fees honest agents earn are the nectar that makes long-term honesty more profitable than spinning up a thousand disposable clones.
